prompt: Some people argue that thanks to the widespread accessibility of the internet, libraries are no longer necessary. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often claimed that the prevalence of the internet has reduced the need for libraries. I disagree with this statement because numerous people still prefer reading physical materials, and these institutions provide access to publications through legitimate and authorised sources.

There are many individuals who would rather read and obtain printed books than read from a screen. With this method, they can focus solely on reading instead of getting distracted by notifications or pop-up ads. Moreover, many people, especially those who use electronic devices for work, consider reading a tangible book to be a break from looking at screens. For example, in South Korea, some public libraries have introduced phone-free reading spaces where visitors are encouraged to put away their electronic devices and read printed works without digital distractions. Thus, such facilities remain valuable for individuals who wish to maintain their reading habits.

Although reading or searching for specific data on the internet can be more convenient than going to a library, the latter ensures that the information and reading materials are obtained from legitimate sources. This is especially important when the knowledge being sought is contained in an ancient or rare book, as it may be difficult to determine whether information found online is accurate or reliable. Furthermore, some may choose not to pay for online publications when unauthorised or stolen versions are available on the internet, allowing them to access these works without purchasing them. Although this violates copyright laws, in contrast, libraries allow people to access legitimate copies of such materials for free. For instance, since 2024, to encourage citizens to read more and use legitimate sources for free, the Saudi Ministry of Culture has established public reading facilities in many neighbourhoods in Riyadh.

In conclusion, I strongly believe in the importance of libraries, which allow people to access physical reading materials in a legitimate and authorised way.
